consensus_summary: Primary consensus identifies 'the life' (esp. zōē) as eternal/divine life given through and embodied in Christ himself (often a christological title), with present and future dimensions; covenantal/OT law readings appear only as secondary alternatives.
book_summary: Covenant existence — the life the law produces.
consensus_core_identification: Christ himself / eternal life in Christ
book_core_identification: covenant existence produced by the law
boundary_disagreement: Consensus ranks the Deuteronomic/Levitical 'choose life / live in them' reading as a common but non-primary alternative; the book elevates law-produced covenant existence to the sole core and subordinates or re-reads the christological texts under it.
material_contradiction: Book makes the law the producer of 'the life'; consensus (and the book's own common-view note) makes Christ the source/embodiment of that life. These cannot both be the primary referent of 'the life' without replacement.
rationale: Minimum cores are non-equivalent: consensus centers on the person and gift of Christ; the book replaces that center with an existence generated by Torah. Although the covenantal reading is listed among consensus alternatives, the book treats it as the definition of the term while explicitly noting the christological view as merely 'commonly taught.' Accepting the book therefore requires rejecting the consensus core identification rather than merely narrowing or refining its boundaries. Shared verses (John 14:6, Deut 30) do not erase the replaced referent.
strongest_objection: The definite-article form 'the life' plus John 14:6 / 11:25 are overwhelmingly treated as christological across the consensus; the book's own common-view note concedes this, so the law-production claim lacks independent support from the printed citations alone and conflicts with standard NT teaching that life is not of the law.
